info.name: Ratios API
info.description: Postman-only testing toolkit for the Ratios API. Pairs with TESTING_PLAN.md. Run '00 - Smoke Test' for a fast health check, or the full collection via Collection Runner for deeper coverage. Uses the 'Ratios API - Sandbox' environment for all variables/secrets.

item.name: 00 - Smoke Test (core happy path)
item.description: Fast end-to-end health check covering the most common real-world flow: create client -> update client -> create client workspace -> create task -> update task -> cleanup. Run this whenever you need a quick 'is auth + the API still behaving' check (e.g. after a token refresh, or as a Newman CI health check) without running the full edge-case suite. Self-contained: cleans up everything it creates.

item.name: 3. Create client workspace (project)
item.description: Ratios has no resource literally named 'workspace' in the docs -- 'projects' (Projekter), a project record linked to a client, is the closest match and is what this step targets. Confirm with Ratios/the team if 'client workspace' is meant to be something else (e.g. a client group or statusliste).

item.name: Delete Client (soft delete)
item.description: After deletion, confirm the follow-up GET behavior (404 vs. 200-with-deleted-flag) against TESTING_PLAN.md open question #5 and adjust the assertion below once confirmed.

item.name: per_page=201 (above max - confirm clamp vs. reject)
item.description: Docs say max per_page is 200 but don't say what happens above it. This request documents whichever behavior is observed -- update the test assertion once confirmed: either the response is clamped to <=200 records, or the API returns a 4xx.

item.name: page beyond last (expect empty data, not an error)

exec: const names = json.data.map(r => r.company_name).filter(n => n !== undefined && n !== null);
const names = json.data.map(r => r.company_name).filter(n => n !== undefined && n !== null);
pm.test('only requested fields are returned', () => pm.expect(onlyAllowedFields).to.be.true);
pm.test('all rows match city', () => pm.expect(json.data.every(r => r.city === 'København')).to.be.true);
pm.test('no row has excluded city', () => pm.expect(json.data.every(r => r.city !== 'København')).to.be.true);
pm.test('all rows have null/empty email', () => pm.expect(json.data.every(r => !r.email)).to.be.true);
pm.test('all rows have an allowed status', () => pm.expect(json.data.every(r => ['draft', 'sent'].includes(r.status))).to.be.true);

item.name: Create User (profiles/create-user) - admin/owner only
item.description: send_welcome_email is deliberately false so test runs never email a real inbox.

item.name: Pagination walk - all clients (run via Collection Runner)
item.description: Postman-native replacement for a 'walk every page' sync loop. Self-loops via pm.execution.setNextRequest until a page comes back empty, accumulating sync_total_count. Run this single request directly (it re-queues itself) or include it in a Collection Runner pass. Uses per_page=200 (the documented max) to minimize round-trips.

exec: console.log(`Pagination walk complete. Total client records: ${total}`);

item.name: Incremental sync - clients updated since last_sync_at
item.description: Pattern for polling-based incremental sync. `updated_at` is assumed based on common convention -- confirm the real field name empirically (TESTING_PLAN.md open question #5 / Phase 1) and adjust the filter.* param name here if different. Set last_sync_at in the environment to your last successful sync timestamp.

item.name: Rate limit probe - read this before running
item.description: Not a scripted burst -- Postman's per-request scripting isn't a great fit for a tight timed loop, and an uncontrolled burst against production is exactly what we want to avoid. To probe for rate limits: point this request's environment at the SANDBOX tenant only, then use Collection Runner with an explicit inter-request delay (e.g. Runner 'Delay' setting, 250ms) and a set iteration count (e.g. 20), watching for 429 responses or X-RateLimit-*/Retry-After headers in the Runner results. Record findings back into TESTING_PLAN.md section 7. This request body is a harmless read (GET /api/tenants) suitable for that Runner pass.

item.name: 99 - Cleanup
item.description: Run after a full Collection Runner pass, or periodically, to find any test data left behind by a crashed/interrupted run (the smoke test and per-folder CRUD requests clean up after themselves on the happy path, but a failed assertion mid-run can skip a later Delete step).

item.name: Find leftover test clients (by prefix)
item.description: Lists any client whose company_name starts with the configured test_prefix. Review the results, then delete each via '02 - Clients > Delete Client (soft delete)' with client_id_created set to the id in question, or via the Ratios UI.

exec: console.log('Leftover test clients:', json.data.map(r => ({ id: r.id, company_name: r.company_name })));
console.log('Leftover test tasks:', json.data.map(r => ({ id: r.id, title: r.title })));
console.log('Leftover test projects:', json.data.map(r => ({ id: r.id, title: r.title })));
